title: Maximum AB and BC Swap Operations
statement:
You are given a string `S` of length `N` consisting only of the characters `A`, `B` and `C`.

In one operation you must perform exactly one of the following on **adjacent** characters:

- replace an occurrence of `AB` with `BA`;
- replace an occurrence of `BC` with `CB`.

You may choose which operation and which position at every step. Find the **maximum number of operations** that can be performed on the string. It can be proven that this maximum is always finite.

Note that the answer can exceed the range of a 32-bit integer.
inputFormat:
The first line contains the integer `N`.
The second line contains the string `S` of length `N`.
outputFormat: Print a single integer: the maximum number of operations.
constraints: S consists only of the characters A, B and C

examples.explanation: Either swap AB to get BAC, or swap BC to get ACB. In both cases no allowed pair remains, so only one operation is possible.

The first B and the last B can never move: the first has an A to its right (BA is not an operation) and the last has nothing to its right. The middle B can either pass the A on its left (BBACB) or the C on its right (BACBB), but not both, because after one move the other neighbour is the wrong letter. After either move no AB or BC pair remains, so the answer is 1.
ABAB -> BAAB -> BABA -> BBAA uses three operations, and no pair AB or BC remains.

hints: An A and a C never swap with each other, and an operation can never be undone, so only the relative order of A and B (and of B and C) changes. Think about what each individual B can do.
A B can only move left past A's or right past C's. Once it has moved left, an A sits to its right, so it can no longer go right (and vice versa). So each B commits to one direction.

Ignore the B's and look at the A/C sequence. For a B sitting in a gap of that sequence, it can pass the run of consecutive A's immediately before the gap or the run of consecutive C's immediately after it. Each B contributes the larger of the two runs; sum over all B's.
